reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism of ADAPT VTCS operates through temporal counterfactual generation, where a player’s initiation time is shifted ±1 s to simulate alternative tactical decisions. Each shift generates a scenario scored using a pitch-control value function, which quantifies spatial influence. The difference between the actual scenario (ξ=0) and the best counterfactual (ξ≠0) yields V_timing, a continuous measure of suboptimality. This is grounded in a discrete-time dynamical system where player states evolve according to kinematic rules. The frame-level value function V_frame aggregates local pitch-control fields over a reachable region Ω(t), approximating a disc-player rendezvous circle. The scenario value V_scenario(ξ) captures the maximum influence over a 15-frame window, enabling temporal smoothing. The timing score V_timing = V_scenario(0) − max_{ξ≠0} V_scenario(ξ) reflects the degradation in tactical value due to mis-timing. This framework assumes static defender behavior and linear motion, limiting its applicability when defenders react dynamically or when motion is non-linear. The method is robust to kinematic noise but sensitive to inaccuracies in disc trajectory or player velocity estimation.
